entryPointReview: Read nethack-c/upstream/src/do.c:doup() (1298-1347), including each early return, branch order, source message, and the final prev_level(TRUE) call. The active command entry point is cmd.c extcmdlist's '<' row at 1919 and rhack's command dispatch at 3714; js/cmd.js runUpCommand routes that key through failClosedCommand to doup(). The C helper calls consumed by doup() are u_rooted(), stucksteed(TRUE), u_stuck_cannot_go(), near_capacity(), ledger_no(), and next_to_u(); the first five and next_to_u() already have source-owned ports, and the incomplete stucksteed/u_stuck_cannot_go message branches are now implemented and awaited. climb_pit() is void and its result is discarded, so the pit path records note_unported('trap.c climb_pit') and returns ECMD_TIME. The D:1 yes path calls dungeon.c prev_level(TRUE), whose D:1 branch calls end.c done(ESCAPED); JavaScript passes the existing done() implementation into prev_level(). Other command paths into doup() use the same function-pointer dispatch or queued-command handler in cmd.c.

functions.name: doup
functions.sourceReview: Compared the entire do.c doup() body (1298-1347) with js/do.js doup() in source order: stairway lookup; DIR_UP setup; rooted and pit guards; missing/wrong staircase refusal; stuck-steed and held/swallowed guards; capacity message and turn debit; D:1 debug-fuzzer return; y_n() query with C's exact double space and 'y' comparison; adjacent-pet gate; at_ladder set/clear around prev_level(TRUE); ECMD_TIME return. doup() now records the discarded void climb_pit() call as note_unported('trap.c climb_pit') and keeps C's ECMD_TIME result. Its value-consuming u_stuck_cannot_go() and stucksteed() callees now implement their complete C return and message branches in js/do.js and js/steed.js; the existing helpers u_rooted(), near_capacity(), ledger_no(), and next_to_u() remain wired. Read dungeon.c prev_level() (1518-1543); its D:1 no-Amulet branch awaits injected done(ESCAPED), while existing same-dungeon and branch transitions still use goto_level().

callers.source: cmd.c:1919 binds '<' to doup(); cmd.c:3714 dispatches the '<' key to that handler. js/cmd.js runUpCommand() calls doup(state) through failClosedCommand().

supplementalSourceRecords.name: u_stuck_cannot_go
supplementalSourceRecords.sourceReview: Compared the complete C helper: when u.ustuck is set, it returns TRUE and reports whether the hero is being held, swallowed, or engulfed unless the hero sticks; a sticky hero releases its holder and continues to FALSE. With no holder it returns FALSE. The JavaScript helper preserves the conditional message and return branches, uses the existing sticks(), mon_nam(), and set_ustuck() ports, and is awaited by both command callers.

callers.source: do.c:1221 calls u_stuck_cannot_go("down") and returns ECMD_TIME when true.
do.c:1321 calls u_stuck_cannot_go("up") and returns ECMD_TIME when true.

matchingSyntheticRanges.executedBranch: doup reaches the helper with no holder; it returns FALSE and the D:1 confirmation branch follows.
doup reaches the helper with no holder; it returns FALSE before prev_level() escapes.

supplementalSourceRecords.entryPointCoverageStillMissing: The cited matching ranges do not exercise a held/swallowed/engulfed refusal or the sticky-holder release branch.

supplementalSourceRecords.name: stucksteed
supplementalSourceRecords.sourceReview: Compared the complete C function: if a steed exists and is helpless it prints the cannot-move message and returns TRUE; when checkfeeding is true and the steed is eating it prints the eating message and returns TRUE; otherwise it returns FALSE. The JavaScript implementation preserves those checks and awaits the corresponding pline output.

callers.source: apply.c:2006 calls stucksteed(FALSE) for non-magic jumping while mounted.
hack.c:2815 calls stucksteed(FALSE) before mounted movement.

matchingSyntheticRanges.executedBranch: doup calls stucksteed(TRUE) with no steed; it returns FALSE before the D:1 prompt.
doup calls stucksteed(TRUE) with no steed; it returns FALSE before the D:1 escape.

supplementalSourceRecords.entryPointCoverageStillMissing: The cited matching ranges do not exercise a mounted steed that is helpless or eating, so neither message/refusal branch has matching recorded play here.

supplementalSourceRecords.name: prev_level
supplementalSourceRecords.sourceReview: Compared the full C function and traced its only C caller. It marks an up stairway traversed; an upward dungeon-branch crossing on D:1 without the Amulet calls done(ESCAPED), while other branch transitions and ordinary ascent construct the source destination and call goto_level(). The JavaScript branch awaits done(ESCAPED) and retains the existing transition paths.

callers.source: do.c:1341 calls prev_level(TRUE) after the pet gate, setting and then clearing ga.at_ladder. JavaScript passes the existing done() and goto_level() operations to prev_level().

matchingSyntheticRanges.executedBranch: doup enters prev_level(TRUE) on the upward dungeon branch at D:1 without the Amulet; prev_level calls done(ESCAPED).

supplementalSourceRecords.entryPointCoverageStillMissing: This range validates the D:1 escape arm. It does not cover ordinary same-dungeon ascent, an upward branch transition away from D:1, or the D:1 branch case with the Amulet.

correctionCoverageNote: These supplemental records cover helper functions implemented or completed as necessary value-consuming callees of the assigned doup port. The formal functions array remains scoped to the queued do.c:doup goal because worker delivery validation binds that array to one C file.
